criteria_results.criterion_text: `KeycloakTokenResolver` in `src/study_tutor/http/auth_keycloak.py` implements `TokenResolver` and validates signature, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`/`nbf` (60s leeway), and an RS256-only algorithm allowlist
criteria_results.evidence: KeycloakTokenResolver implements the TokenResolver protocol with async resolve() method. Uses PyJWT.decode() with algorithms=['RS256'] allowlist, validates issuer via issuer= parameter, audience via audience= parameter, exp/nbf with leeway=60 from settings. Tests verify RS256 validation, alg:none rejection, HS256 rejection, issuer validation, audience validation, expiration, and not-yet-valid handling.

criteria_results.criterion_text: The `student_id` claim (name from `OIDCSettings.student_claim`) is extracted only **after** validation; a missing claim raises `Unauthenticated`, never a 500
criteria_results.evidence: Claim extraction happens in Step 3 of resolve() method, after all PyJWT validation passes. Missing/empty/non-string student_id claim raises Unauthenticated with descriptive message. Test test_missing_student_claim_raises_unauthenticated verifies this behavior.

criteria_results.criterion_text: Every negative path (bad signature, wrong issuer, wrong audience, expired, not-yet-valid, `alg:none`/HS256, unknown kid, unreachable JWKS, garbage token) raises `Unauthenticated` and raises no unexpected error
criteria_results.evidence: All PyJWT exceptions (ExpiredSignatureError, ImmatureSignatureError, InvalidIssuerError, InvalidAudienceError, InvalidAlgorithmError, InvalidSignatureError, DecodeError, InvalidTokenError) are caught and converted to Unauthenticated. PyJWKClientError from JWKS fetch failures also raises Unauthenticated. Final catch-all Exception handler ensures fail-closed behavior. Tests cover all negative paths: bad signature, unknown kid, wrong issuer/audience, expired, not-yet-valid, alg:none, HS256, unreachable JWKS, garbage token.

criteria_results.criterion_text: Issuer used for `iss` validation stays the ts.net name even when the JWKS fetch URL is overridden to a tailnet IP (KC-D2)
criteria_results.evidence: KeycloakTokenResolver.__init__ stores expected_issuer=settings.issuer (the ts.net name) separately from jwks_url. PyJWT.decode() uses issuer=self.expected_issuer for validation, not derived from JWKS URL. Test test_issuer_validation_uses_ts_net_name verifies that tokens with ts.net issuer pass validation while tokens with IP issuer fail, even when JWKS URL is the IP address.
